plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (AR-Matched Bragg Stack with Impedance Grading) based on feedback directives. Previous iteration achieved best_target_score of 0.6085 with 20 optimized layers. This refinement implements the prescribed initialization strategy: anchor AR section (layers 0-3) to quarter-wavelength estimates at 1547.5 nm center wavelength, while maintaining full optimization freedom for interior Bragg reflectors (layers 4-19). Three complementary routes explore different AR anchoring strategies and layer count variations to reduce combinatorial entropy while preserving the verified impedance grading principle.

routes.title: QW-AR-Anchored 20-Layer Bragg Stack with Gradient Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Anchoring the first 4 AR-matching layers to quarter-wavelength thickness estimates at the telecom band center (1547.5 nm) will reduce early-round search entropy and enable the optimizer to more efficiently discover high-transmittance solutions in the 1530-1565 nm band while maintaining visible reflectance through the remaining 16 Bragg layers.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave AR matching at the passband center wavelength reduces initial parameter space volume for the impedance-graded entrance section, allowing the optimizer to focus computational budget on tuning the Bragg reflector section for visible band rejection.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | [HfO2 | SiO2] x 8 | Fused Silica substrate. Total 20 coating layers: 4 AR-matching entrance layers + 16 Bragg reflector layers (8 high-low pairs).
design_variables: All 20 layer thicknesses (nm) with layers 0-3 initialized to quarter-wavelength estimates at 1547.5 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses should remain within typical deposition tolerances (50-400 nm range)
theory_basis: Quarter-wave impedance matching theory for reducing Fresnel reflection at dielectric interfaces
Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
Bragg reflector theory for high-reflectance band formation
expected_advantages: Reduced search space dimensionality for AR section accelerates convergence
Quarter-wave initialization provides physically meaningful starting point
Maintains full optimization freedom for Bragg section to tune visible rejection
known_risks: Quarter-wave anchoring may constrain AR section from discovering superior non-quarter-wave solutions
Fixed 20-layer count may not be optimal for this dual-band requirement
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (20 coating layers total). Initialize layers 0-3 (first 4 layers) to quarter-wavelength optical thickness at 1547.5 nm center wavelength (HfO2: n≈2.05, target physical thickness ~189 nm; SiO2: n≈1.46, target physical thickness ~265 nm). Allow all 20 layer thicknesses to be optimized by gradient-based optimizer with bounds 50-400 nm. Evaluate coherent plane-wave transmittance and reflectance across 400-700 nm and 1530-1565 nm bands at normal incidence. Objective: maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to anchor AR section (layers 0-3) to quarter-wavelength estimates at central operating frequency while maintaining full search freedom for interior Bragg reflectors (layers 4-19). This reduces early-round combinatorial entropy compared to route_03's unconstrained initialization.

routes.title: QW-AR-Anchored 24-Layer Bragg Stack with Extended Reflector Section
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing the Bragg reflector section from 16 to 20 layers (24 total coating layers) while maintaining quarter-wave AR anchoring for layers 0-3 will improve visible band reflectance without degrading telecom band transmittance, as additional Bragg pairs increase stopband depth.
routes.design_principle: Extended Bragg reflector section provides more degrees of freedom for visible band rejection while quarter-wave AR anchoring maintains efficient telecom band coupling. Layer count increase from 20 to 24 remains within 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | [HfO2 | SiO2] x 10 | Fused Silica substrate. Total 24 coating layers: 4 AR-matching entrance layers + 20 Bragg reflector layers (10 high-low pairs).
design_variables: All 24 layer thicknesses (nm) with layers 0-3 initialized to quarter-wavelength estimates at 1547.5 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain total optical thickness within deposition practicality
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thicknesses should remain within typical deposition tolerances (50-400 nm range)
Increased layer count may increase deposition time and stress accumulation
theory_basis: Bragg reflector stopband depth increases with number of layer pairs
Quarter-wave impedance matching theory for dielectric interfaces
Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Additional 4 Bragg layers provide more design freedom for visible band rejection
Quarter-wave AR anchoring maintains telecom band transmittance efficiency
Tests whether layer count increase improves dual-band performance trade-off
known_risks: Additional layers increase deposition complexity and potential stress
May not improve target_score if 20-layer stack already near-optimal for this material pair
Increased absorption losses in extended stack may reduce telecom transmittance

routes.title: QW-AR-Anchored 20-Layer Stack with Asymmetric HfO2/SiO2 Index Matching
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Using asymmetric quarter-wave anchoring where HfO2 layers are anchored to quarter-wave at 1547.5 nm but SiO2 layers in the AR section are anchored to half-wave at 1547.5 nm will provide better impedance grading while maintaining the same 20-layer topology as route_03.
routes.design_principle: Asymmetric AR section initialization (HfO2 at quarter-wave, SiO2 at half-wave) creates a more gradual effective index transition from air to the Bragg reflector section, potentially improving telecom band transmittance without increasing layer count.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | [HfO2 | SiO2] x 8 | Fused Silica substrate. Total 20 coating layers: 4 AR-matching entrance layers + 16 Bragg reflector layers (8 high-low pairs). Same topology as route_03_refine_01 but different initialization strategy.
design_variables: All 20 layer thicknesses (nm) with layers 0,2 (HfO2) initialized to quarter-wave at 1547.5 nm, layers 1,3 (SiO2) initialized to half-wave at 1547.5 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Achieve smoother effective index gradient in AR section
manufacturing_considerations: SiO2 half-wave layers will be ~530 nm, within deposition capability
Same layer count as route_03 maintains manufacturing parity
theory_basis: Effective medium theory for graded-index antireflection
Quarter-wave and half-wave impedance transformation principles
Transfer matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
expected_advantages: Asymmetric initialization may provide better impedance matching than symmetric quarter-wave
Tests whether SiO2 layer thickness in AR section is critical design parameter
Maintains 20-layer manufacturing simplicity while exploring initialization strategy
known_risks: Half-wave SiO2 layers (~530 nm) may exceed typical deposition uniformity tolerances
Asymmetric initialization may not converge as reliably as symmetric quarter-wave
May not improve over route_03_refine_01 if symmetric quarter-wave is already near-optimal
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric thin-film stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (20 coating layers total). Initialize layers 0 and 2 (HfO2) to quarter-wavelength optical thickness at 1547.5 nm (target physical thickness ~189 nm). Initialize layers 1 and 3 (SiO2) to half-wavelength optical thickness at 1547.5 nm (target physical thickness ~530 nm). Allow all 20 layer thicknesses to be optimized by gradient-based optimizer with bounds 50-600 nm (expanded upper bound for half-wave SiO2). Evaluate coherent plane-wave transmittance and reflectance across 400-700 nm and 1530-1565 nm bands at normal incidence. Objective: maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Tests asymmetric initialization strategy within same 20-layer topology as route_03_refine_01. Complements previous routes by exploring whether SiO2 layer thickness in AR section should differ from HfO2 for better impedance grading.

research_influence: Evidence ID s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the prioritization of 1530-1565 nm transmittance in all route objectives. No literature evidence was found for specific multilayer design strategies, so all routes are theory-based using quarter-wave impedance matching and Bragg reflector principles.
unresolved_decisions: Optimal layer count between 20 and 30 for this dual-band requirement remains unknown - route_03_refine_02 tests 24 layers as intermediate point
Whether symmetric or asymmetric AR section initialization provides better convergence is untested - routes 03_refine_01 and 03_refine_03 compare these strategies
Exact quarter-wave vs non-quarter-wave AR layer thicknesses remain open optimization variables - all routes allow full thickness optimization after initialization
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
